# Stone Steps 50K and 27K Trail Run: Full Site Content

> Plain-text copy of the key pages of https://stonesteps50k.com, the public site for the Stone Steps 50K and 27K Trail Run in Mt. Airy Forest, Cincinnati, Ohio. Everything below is taken from the live site. Date, fees, start times and entry caps are as published on the site and change by year, so confirm them on the site or on RunSignUp before relying on them.

Index of pages: https://stonesteps50k.com/llms.txt

---

## Home (https://stonesteps50k.com/)

Tagline: "Cincinnati's longest running ultra marathon." The site describes the race as the 24th year, with single-track loops through Mt. Airy Forest, about 5,200 feet of climbing, and an aid station every time you come back through The Oval. The page also states: since 2003, USATF sanctioned, big and small loops alternating.

Next running, as published on the site: Sunday, October 25, 2026, the 24th running, Mt. Airy Forest, Cincinnati, OH.

### 50K (the full ultra)
- 30.8 miles, 7 loops: four 5.3 mile loops alternating with three 3.2 mile loops.
- Start 8:00 am. Trekkers may start at 7:00 am.
- Entry cap: 120.
- Fees as published: $35 through January 31, $50 from February 1 to September 30, $55 from October 1 to race day.
- Includes: T-shirt, timing chip, aid station every loop. USATF sanctioned.

### 27K (the fun run)
- 17 miles, 4 loops: two 5.3 mile loops alternating with two 3.2 mile loops, turning for home at 17 miles.
- Start 8:30 am. Trekkers may start at 8:00 am and are ineligible for age group and overall awards.
- Entry cap: 130.
- Fees as published: $30 through January 31, $40 from February 1 to September 30, $45 from October 1 to race day.
- Includes: T-shirt, timing chip, aid station every loop. USATF sanctioned.

The site says prices go up after January 31 and again after September 30. The Contact page adds that fees are plus a processing fee.

### The climbing
About 5,200 feet of climbing. The Oval sits near the top of the course, so every loop drops away from it and climbs back. The site says the final half mile of the big loops climbs at least 170 feet, four times over. 10,344 feet of total elevation change, measured from USGS 1 m LiDAR along a recorded run of the course.

### What to expect
- Hilly trail with roots, rocks and the occasional tree blow down.
- Aid at the end of every loop; on the 50K you pass through aid seven times and drop bags stay in one place all day.
- Mt. Airy Forest is 1,469.9 acres, which the site says is larger than Central Park's 843 acres.
- Every year the race donates the net proceeds (over $2000, as the site words it) to Cincinnati Parks.

### Race-day schedule as published
- 7:00 am: 50K trekker start (optional early start)
- 8:00 am: 50K start, seven loops
- 8:00 am: 27K trekker start, ineligible for awards
- 8:30 am: 27K start, four loops
- 4:30 pm: course closes (approximate)
- Packet pickup, pre-race briefing and awards show "TBC" (to be confirmed) on the site, so no times are given here.
- Packet pickup is at The Oval, Area 13.
- Parking: "There is enough parking," but park close together and only within The Oval, not before it. The site links to directions to The Oval.

### Course records shown on the home page
- Men 50K: David Riddle, 3:40:56, 2011
- Women 50K: Katie Ruhlman, 4:27:23, 2020
- Men 27K: David Riddle, 1:59:32, 2017
- Women 27K: Katie Ruhlman, 2:28:40, 2021

### Race director
David Corfman has directed the race for over twenty years, according to the site. It describes him as the 34th person to finish 100 hundred-mile ultramarathons. Questions about parking, packet pickup and the briefing can be sent to him through the Contact page.

### Between race days
The site says most of what happens between race days happens in the Facebook group: trail conditions, training runs, carpools, race week updates and photos. Group: https://www.facebook.com/groups/1103063513072311/

### Sponsors and partners
Logos shown on the home page (taken from image descriptions): Altra Running, Cincinnati Parks, Fleet Feet, and USATF (sanctioned event).

---

## Course (https://stonesteps50k.com/course/)

Big and small loops out of The Oval, single track through Mt. Airy Forest, with an aid station every time you come back through the start.

### Loop order
Long and short loops alternate: long 5.3 mi, short 3.2, long 5.3, short 3.2, long 5.3, short 3.2, long 5.3. Cumulative miles at The Oval: 5.3, 8.5, 13.8, 17, 22.3, 25.5, then the 50K finish. The 27K covers the first four loops and finishes at 17 miles. The 50K covers all seven.

### Aid, start and finish, cutoff
- Aid is at the end of every loop. Aid is only at The Oval, so a long loop is five plus miles between refills.
- Start and finish: The Oval, Area 13, inside Mt. Airy Forest, for both distances. The 50K goes at 8:00 am, the 27K at 8:30.
- Cutoff: the course closes at approximately 4:30 pm, eight and a half hours after the 50K start.

### Elevation and map
10,344 feet of total elevation change, measured from USGS 1 m LiDAR along a recorded run of the course. The page has an interactive 3D map drawn from that recorded run, with basemap from USGS The National Map.

### Race-day weather by year (as published)

### What to bring (the site's suggestions)
- Trail shoes with real lugs: roots, rocks and wet leaves in late October.
- A handheld or a vest, since aid is only at The Oval.
- One drop bag, which stays at The Oval all day and is passed every loop.
- Layers you can shed: an October morning in Cincinnati starts cold and rarely stays that way.

### Watching
Everything happens at The Oval: the start, the finish, the aid station, and the end of every loop. A spectator can see a runner seven times on the 50K and four times on the 27K. A long loop is 5.3 miles and a short one is 3.2. The site says most runners are back through in somewhere between half an hour and an hour and a quarter.

## Contact (https://stonesteps50k.com/contact/)

A contact form for the race director, David Corfman, covering course or race day questions, registration or transfer, volunteering, sponsorship, results corrections and anything else. The Facebook group is where the site says course conditions, carpools and last-minute changes get posted.

Start line: The Oval, Area 13, Mt. Airy Forest, Cincinnati, OH. Directions to The Oval are linked from the page. For out-of-town visitors the site says Mt. Airy Forest is close to both downtown Cincinnati and the airport area, and a couple of miles from I-75 and I-74 off Colerain Avenue.

### Answers the site publishes
- What does my entry include? A race t-shirt and a timing chip, plus aid at the end of every loop. Entries also fund the annual donation to Cincinnati Parks.
- Where does the race start? The Oval, Area 13, inside Mt. Airy Forest. Both distances start and finish there, and you pass back through it at the end of every loop.
- How much is it? The 50K is $35 through January 31, $50 from February 1 to September 30 and $55 from October 1 to race day. The 27K is $30, $40 and $45 on the same dates. Both plus a processing fee. The 50K is capped at 120 entries and the 27K at 130.
- What time does it start? The 50K at 8:00 am and the 27K at 8:30 am. Trekkers may start an hour earlier in each case, and 27K trekkers are not eligible for age group or overall awards. The course closes at about 4:30 pm.
- What is the course like? Hilly single track with roots, rocks and the occasional tree blow down. The 50K is four 5.3 mile loops alternating with three 3.2 mile loops, for about 5,200 feet of climbing and 10,344 feet of total elevation change.
- Where are past results? The records page carries course and age-group records for both distances. The complete archive, including years this site does not hold, lives on RunSignUp.

---

## Privacy (https://stonesteps50k.com/privacy/)

Summary of what the page says; last reviewed September 2026 per the page.
- Results pages publish finishing data for every race the archive has records for, back to 2003: name, finish time, distance, placing, and where recorded an age, a gender category and a home city and state.
- To be removed from the results pages, email rd@stonesteps50k.com with the name and the year. No form and no reason are needed.
- The contact form stores your name, email, subject and message, the date and time, your browser user agent, and a two letter country code, in the race's own database on Cloudflare. It is used only for replying. Cloudflare Turnstile guards the form; the site does not store your IP address.
- Page visits are measured with Google Analytics, which sets cookies (_ga and _ga_ plus a stream id). It is not used for advertising.
- The 3D course map loads imagery and terrain tiles from public services, which see your IP address.
- Registration and results are on RunSignUp and the race also has a Facebook group; those sites have their own privacy policies.
- The site says it sells nothing, runs no ads or ad-tracking pixels, has no newsletter, and has no accounts or logins.
